sequence_description: I1 attack: exploit proof/attribute integrity by forging SAML assertions for two distinct upstream principals that share the same email, under a broker config that trusts upstream email. If Keycloak links both to one downstream account, it consumed semantically different proofs as the same subject.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML logins report success (HTTP 200) but no authenticated session/identity can be verified, suggesting the flow may not have actually established a user session (or session handling is broken), preventing assessment of email-based principal collapse.

sequence_description: Replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID containing <OneTimeUse/> twice in the same realm/provider context; second attempt must be rejected. Uses two identities to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
description: [LLM-Judge] Both SAML login attempts returned HTTP 200/success but no authenticated session was established (subsequent identity verification returned 401), suggesting the login endpoint may be reporting success without actually granting access.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Both SAML login attempts returned HTTP 200/success but no authenticated session was established (subsequent identity verification returned 401), suggesting the login endpoint may be reporting success without actually granting access.

sequence_description: Replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID after forcing user-wide logout; second acceptance indicates replay cache not enforced or incorrectly scoped to active sessions only.
